inputs.share_count_basis: Q1 2026 weighted average diluted 279,257,643 (Q1-2026 interim note 5). Held FLAT: SBC expensed in the flows; TMX ran an NCIB again in Q1 2026 (57.5m) after pausing it in FY2024-25 to de-lever from VettaFi.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash flow statement 'Cost of share option plan' 2.0 (X.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:5192). Note 23 total share-based expense 50.6 (FY2024 59.4) is overwhelmingly RSU/PSU/DSU units that are CASH-settled: they are expensed in Compensation and benefits, sit inside reported EBITDA and OCF, and are paid in cash, so they are already charged in the flows. Only the equity-settled option cost is a non-cash add-back and is charged as the SBC line. No net-share settlement, so equity-award taxes are nil.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2024 and FY2025 NCIB repurchases were nil (de-levering after the January 2024 VettaFi acquisition); Q1 2026 repurchased 57.5m. Option dilution is ~0.1% of revenue, so the flat count is essentially self-funding.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:00:00Z regular close (TSX, Friday); Yahoo chart API
inputs.anchor_vintage_warning: Q2 2026 (June) interim was due in early August 2026 but has not been downloaded or extracted into research/X.TO/Extracted; the latest available balance sheet is 31 March 2026. Replace cash, debt and diluted shares with the June 2026 figures when that filing is extracted.
inputs.net_debt_build: 31-Mar-2026: debt current 499.4 + non-current 1,545.4 + credit and liquidity facilities drawn 10.1 + lease liabilities 97.5 = 2,152.4; less cash and cash equivalents 358.6 and marketable securities 143.2 = 501.8. Clearing balances (Balances of Participants and Clearing Members 47,138.4, matched both sides) and participants' tax withholdings 305.9 (matched both sides) are pass-through and excluded. REPO/collateral interest (1,205.1 in FY2025) is presented gross and nets to nil, so it is not in revenue. Some cash supports CDCC/CDS regulatory capital; it is kept in the bridge at face value, a small generosity.
inputs.wacc_rationale: CAD build. Government of Canada 10y ~3.3%; equity risk premium 5.25%; beta 0.85 (exchange operators trade at 0.6-0.8 raw; rounded up for 2025-26 volume-cycle exposure) -> cost of equity ~7.8%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.0% on debentures (after tax ~2.9%). Market-value D/V ~13% (2.15bn debt vs ~14.8bn market cap). WACC ~7.2%, set at 7.5% and held identical across scenarios: cyclical volume risk is charged in the bear flows, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities 97.5 sit in total_debt; lease principal (9.5 in FY2025) is NOT deducted from the flows; ROU renewal charged by adding ~0.5pp to the capex path.
inputs.nci_treatment: BOX Holdings (US equity options exchange) is consolidated at 47.9% economic / 51.4% voting; 52.1% NCI took 62.3 of FY2025 net income (45.4 FY2024) and 81.7 of dividends. Flows are consolidated 100%, so the NCI is deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at estimated fair value (see equity_bridge), not at book (214.3).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US adaptations (CAD WACC, lease treatment A, BOX NCI in bridge). Routing: TMX is an operating company - listings, trading, clearing fees, Trayport subscriptions, VettaFi index/data licensing and market-data fees. Its clearing houses (CDCC, CDS) carry participant collateral, but those balances are matched pass-through items (REPO interest presented gross and netted to nil; participant balances equal on both sides of the balance sheet); TMX takes no deposits and earns no spread on its own balance sheet, so the bank (residual income) route does not apply. Net debt is corporate debt only. FCF basis: reported OCF is unlevered (interest paid is in financing, interest received in investing), so no interest-income strip is needed and TMX is net-debt in any case. FY2025 OCF includes +12.7 movement in participants' tax withholdings, a pass-through item; last_fcf keeps the contract identity (643.6 - 2.0 - 0), and the component build, which ties FY0 owner FCF to ~609 after a full unlevered cash tax, is the number that drives value. Non-recurring items stripped from the base: FY2017 NGX sale gain, FY2022 other income 177.9, FY2024 VettaFi remeasurement gain 57.1, FY2025 FX loss on intercompany loans and contingent-consideration FV in net finance costs (below EBITDA anyway), and Q1 2026 net legal-settlement income 83.8 (Note 9; cash 91.1 received - this explains the Q1 2026 net income of 224.6 flagged by the parser; it is in the March cash balance, so it is not also projected). Pending: Cboe Australia + Cboe Canada acquisition for US$300m (C$409.9m) announced 22-Apr-2026, subject to regulatory approval - treated as value-neutral (neither the cash out nor the acquired revenue is modelled). Analysis.json was not present at build time; cross-check scenario narratives against it when it lands.

equity_bridge.item: BOX non-controlling interest (52.1%) at estimated fair value
equity_bridge.note: Mid-cycle NCI earnings ~55 (FY2024 45.4, FY2025 62.3 on record US options volumes) x 17x P/E. Book NCI 202.6 (31-Mar-2026) would understate the claim ~4.6x. FY2025 Note 26 (X.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:7727).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: organic revenue growth (FY2025 ex-acquisitions +15% was a high-volume year; long-run organic ~7-9%), consistent with management's long-term revenue CAGR objective (High/Strong/Market growth by segment; objectives table is an image not captured in the extract). Equity CAGR rejected: TMX pays ~50% of adjusted EPS as dividends and funded VettaFi with debt, so book value understates the compounding of the business.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5.7-6.1%) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (14.7-15.4%, flattered by the January 2024 VettaFi consolidation and Newsfile/iNDEX/Bond Indices/ETF Stream/Verity) and from GAAP EPS (3yr -8.4% off a FY2022 base inflated by 177.9 other income; FY2025 GAAP EPS 1.49 vs adjusted 2.13 because of ~114 of acquired-intangible amortization and FX losses).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = OCF - capex - lease principal - option cost (FY2020 ~333.5, FY2022 ~380.5, FY2025 ~619.4 after also removing the 12.7 tax-withholding pass-through). Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within 0.3pp because SBC is ~0.1% of revenue: the cash-settled units are already in OCF. Historical FCF CAGRs include the debt-funded VettaFi acquisition (~C$1.13bn cash, FY2024) and so overstate organic growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +12%: Q1 2026 revenue +16.5% y/y (some inorganic from Bond Indices/ETF Stream/Verity) on strong equity and derivatives volumes; assume the back half cools. Then decelerates from ~8% toward 4%, the lower end of management's long-term objectives, as the 2025-26 volume tailwind fades and growth rests on Trayport, VettaFi indices, data and MX/CDCC.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 reported EBITDA margin 55.4% (55.5% before the 2.0 option cost); FY2025 one-offs in opex were 58.6 (acquisition/integration, litigation 13.6, strategic realignment 12.0, BOX CAT charge 15.3, contingent accruals) - about half treated as recurring because TMX acquires every year. Q1 2026 ran 58.9%. Path 57.5% -> 58.5%: operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base, partly offset by AlphaX US build-out and tech spend.
base.tax_rationale: Unlevered CASH rate on book EBIT. FY2023-25 cash taxes paid / EBIT averaged 24.4%; adding back the interest tax shield (unlevered basis) gives ~27%. Statutory ~26.5% plus US (BOX, VettaFi) and UK (Trayport). Book D&A includes ~114/yr of acquired-intangible amortization, mostly non-deductible, so D&A glides down while the rate is held near statutory.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 7.1% was elevated by the Post-Trade Modernization (PTM) project that went live 28-Apr-2025; FY2022-24 ran 4.6-5.5%; Q1 2026 3.4%. Path 6.0% -> 5.5% includes ~0.5pp for right-of-use renewal under lease treatment A.
base.wc_rationale: Receivables-led: FY2025 receivables/prepaids consumed 48.6 against payables +32.1 and deferred revenue +3.3 on +257 revenue. -5% of the revenue increase.

scenario_narratives.base: Exchange franchise compounds at mid-to-high single digits once the 2025-26 volume surge normalizes. TSX/TSXV listings and trading recover cyclically but grow only with Canadian market cap; the growth engines are TMX Trayport (European energy trading network, subscription pricing), TMX VettaFi (index licensing tied to ETF AUM), TMX Datalinx market data, and MX/CDCC derivatives (Canadian rates futures, CORRA). BOX contributes but 52% of it belongs to the NCI. Margins edge up from ~57.5% to ~58.5% on operating leverage. FY2026 +12% on Q1's +16.5%, then 8% fading to 4%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Volumes stay structurally higher (retail options and rates-hedging demand persist), Trayport keeps double-digit growth as European power/gas trading electrifies, VettaFi index royalties ride ETF AUM growth, and AlphaX US plus the pending Cboe Australia/Canada deal extend the franchise beyond Canada. Revenue grows ~15% in FY2026 and stays near 9-10% through the mid-decade; margin reaches 61% as the PTM and cloud migrations stop costing. Terminal multiple 22x reflects a global data-and-infrastructure mix closer to LSEG/ICE.
scenario_narratives.bear: 2025-26 proves to be a cyclical volume peak: a market drawdown in FY2027 cuts trading, clearing and listings revenue and VettaFi AUM-linked fees together (revenue -2%), while the cost base (AlphaX US, tech, regulatory build) does not flex, compressing margin to ~54-55%. Alternative Canadian venues and Cboe/Nasdaq competition take share in cash equities, Trayport faces a well-funded competitor, and the OSC/AMF recognition orders cap clearing-fee pricing. Long-run growth ~3% with a 16x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default) because FY2025-26 results sit on unusually high trading and derivatives volumes, so mean reversion is a live risk rather than a tail; there is no balance-sheet or solvency risk (debt/EBITDA ~2.2x, falling). Base 50% as the central case. Bull 30% (below the 35% default) because it needs several independent things - sustained volumes, Trayport and VettaFi growth, and successful US/Australian expansion - to go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: TMX is a regulated, network-effect exchange and market-infrastructure operator with a quasi-monopoly on Canadian listings, clearing and depository, plus faster-growing global data/energy-trading assets. Valued as an operating company on unlevered owner FCF at a CAD WACC; the clearing balance sheet is pass-through and excluded. SBC is genuinely small on the house basis because the share units are cash-settled and already in EBITDA, so house and street values nearly coincide.
key_risks_to_valuation: Volume cyclicality: FY2025-26 revenue growth was driven by record derivatives (+32%) and equities trading (+20%) volumes; a normalization year is in the bear case.
BOX NCI fair value is an estimate (~935); each 1x on the 17x multiple moves value ~0.20/share.
Terminal value carries most of the value; the 20x cap binds in the base because Gordon at 7.5%/3.0% exceeds it.
Balance sheet anchors are from 31-Mar-2026; the June 2026 interim has not been extracted.
Pending US$300m Cboe Australia/Canada acquisition treated as value-neutral.
Acquisitive capital allocation (VettaFi, Newsfile, iNDEX, Bond Indices, ETF Stream, Verity): the model does not credit future M&A, nor charge for overpaying.
